subject.title: Add optional `name`/`label` field to group config entries

question: Which single public metadata field name and write scope should OpenClaw accept for channel group config entries?
rationale: This changes the public configuration contract and possibly agent-writable config paths, so automation should not choose between `name`, `label`, `description`, aliases, or gateway-tool write scope without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt `name` everywhere
options.body: Use one optional `name?: string` field across relevant group-entry schemas, types, generated metadata, docs, and tests while keeping runtime behavior unchanged.

options.title: Choose another single field
options.body: Pick `label` or `description` instead, but still apply only one canonical field consistently across the same surfaces.

options.title: Decline config metadata
options.body: Keep group entries behavior-only and rely on external notes, channel display labels, or future UI affordances for readability.

recommendation.title: Adopt `name` everywhere
recommendation.body: Use one optional `name?: string` field across relevant group-entry schemas, types, generated metadata, docs, and tests while keeping runtime behavior unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a public config-contract decision, and the strongest history signal for strict config schema ownership points to steipete.
